summary: Specializing in Indology and philosophy, Kunio Harikai earned a BA and PhD degrees at Kyushu University, studying under Seiren Matsunami and Shōren Ihara. He held posts at Saga University (~1976–1986) and Saga Medical School (attested 1991).
Kunio Iwaya studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1963 to 1970 and held a post at Meiji Gakuin University from circa 1972 to 2014.
Kunio Mugitani is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied under Mitsuji Fukunaga. He served as a professor at Kyoto University from circa 1992 to 2012.
Kunio Odaka studied at the University of Tokyo (~1928–1931). He later held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1969) and Sophia University (~1969–1979).

A scholar of Japanology and religious studies, Kunio Yanagita studied law at the University of Tokyo (~1897–1900). His career included posts at the Ministry of Agriculture and Commerce, Permanent Mandates Commission, Tokyo Asahi Shimbun, and Kokugakuin University (~1946–1952).

Philosopher Kuno Fischer studied at the University of Leipzig (~1844–1845) and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1845–1847). He served as a professor at the University of Jena (~1856–1872) and Heidelberg University (~1872–1906).

Philosopher Kuno Lorenz completed his PhD at Kiel University and his habilitation at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg. He held a chair in philosophy at the University of Hamburg (1970) and served as a professor at Saarland University (1974–1998).

Linguist Kuno Meyer studied under Ernst Windisch at the University of Leipzig (~1879–1884). He held academic posts at the University of Liverpool (~1884–1911) and Frederick William University Berlin (~1911–1919).

Specializing in philosophy and Buddhist studies, Kuntala Bhattacharya studied under Prabal Kumar Sen, Shyamapada Misra, and Amita Chatterjee, receiving a PhD from Jadavpur University (attested 2009). She held a post at Rabindra Bharati University (attested 2009).
Kunzang Namgyal studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Kunzang Pelden studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught numerous students, including Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Shechen Gyaltsab.

id: P:Kunzig Shamar Rinpoche Mipham Chokyi Lodro
summary: Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Kunzig Shamar Rinpoche Mipham Chokyi Lodro studied under the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Kalu Rinpoche (1973).

A scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology, Kuo-Pin Chuang completed a PhD at National Chung Hsing University. He held postdoctoral posts at National Taiwan University (2019–2022) and the University of Edinburgh (2022), later becoming a professor at Chung-Hwa Institute.

Kurt A. Behrendt, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, received his PhD from UCLA (~1991–1997). He served at the Metropolitan Museum of Art as Assistant Curator (~2006–2013) and Associate Curator of South Asian Art (~2013).
Working in Indology, Kurt Andrew Johnson earned his PhD from the University of York by 2010, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Jane Moody.
In the field of Buddhist studies, Kurt Bruno Otto Fischer was a pupil of Paul Dahlke (~1921–1928), whom he succeeded in 1928 to serve as leader of Das Buddhistische Haus (~1928–1942).

Working in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, Kurt Friedrich Leidecker earned his PhD from the University of Chicago (~1924–1927). He held professorships at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (1934–1942) and the University of Mary Washington (1948–1973).
Kurt Huber studied philosophy at the University of Munich, completing his PhD (~1913–1917). He held posts there as außerordentlicher Professor in 1926 and received a professorship in 1938.
Kurt Hutten, who worked in religious studies and Indology, completed his PhD at the University of Tübingen (~1926–1930) under doctoral supervisor Jakob Wilhelm Hauer.
Working in Indology and linguistics, Kurt Klemm studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and earned his PhD at the University of Leipzig by 1894 under supervisors Ernst Windisch and Karl Brugmann.
